_meta.description: StoreHub Creative Theme Framework — 8 testable creative angles for ad experiments. Each theme tests a distinct psychological lever. Use this to ensure batches test across multiple themes, not just format/copy variations of the same angle.
_meta.how_to_use: Each iteration should test at least 2-3 themes head-to-head. Assign 2-3 creative variations per theme (same angle, different executions). Declare a theme winner at 10%+ lift on its primary KPI after 7 days / 1000+ impressions. Retire losing themes and double down on winners.

themes.name: Pain Amplification
themes.one_liner: Start inside the merchant's worst moment — no solution yet. Make them feel seen.
themes.core_insight: A merchant who feels understood before being sold to is far more likely to convert than one who sees a product pitch cold. The ad mirrors their reality so precisely that they stop scrolling because it feels personal.
themes.emotional_lever: Recognition — 'That is literally my life right now'
themes.NOT: Stress-to-Success transformation arc (proven to fail in PH — 0 SQLs across 5 variants). This theme STAYS in the pain. The call to action is the only escape offered.
execution_directions: Show a merchant at 2am doing reconciliation. No caption needed beyond one true line.
Recreate a specific peak-hour chaos moment — tablets everywhere, staff shouting, queue out the door.
A checklist of everything they manually manage that StoreHub handles. Just a list. No product shot.
A fake invoice showing all the hidden costs of NOT having a good POS (missed orders, staff errors, overtime).
themes.copy_direction: Lead with the pain, not the product. Second sentence only — offer the exit.
themes.hypothesis: Ads that name a specific merchant pain before introducing any product will drive higher SQL% because they pre-qualify — only merchants who identify with the pain will engage.
themes.known_data: Question hooks ('How much are you paying in delivery fees?') delivered CPL RM37-41 in PH — lowest in dataset. Pain-first framing is directionally validated but never tested as a standalone visual theme.
themes.watch_out: Do not drift into transformation/journey narrative — that killed performance in PH. Stay in the problem.

themes.name: New Chapter
themes.one_liner: Grand opening energy. You've worked for this moment — your tools should match your ambition.
themes.core_insight: Merchants who just opened, renovated, or expanded are at a high-intent, high-emotion decision point. They're spending money and making long-term decisions. An ad that meets them at that milestone — rather than interrupting them with a generic promo — feels relevant, not intrusive.
themes.emotional_lever: Pride + excitement + 'I deserve the best for this moment'
themes.NOT: Generic 'new business discount' promo. This is about the milestone, not the offer. The offer is secondary.
execution_directions: A beautifully renovated empty restaurant just before opening — 'You built something beautiful. Now run it with the best.'
A fake renovation invoice where the POS is the only line item they saved on.
A countdown to opening day visual — everything checked off, POS is the last item.
An owner standing in front of their new signage. One line of copy. No product shot.
themes.copy_direction: Acknowledge the milestone first. Position StoreHub as the final piece that completes their setup.
themes.hypothesis: Life-stage moment targeting (just opened/renovating/expanding) produces higher SQL% than evergreen campaigns because it intercepts the audience at an active purchase decision, not just pain awareness.
themes.known_data: No direct test of milestone-targeting as a creative angle. The 55% off hardware campaign is the offer — this theme determines how to frame it.
themes.watch_out: Avoid making the image look like a stock photo. Must feel like their specific business, not a generic cafe.

themes.name: Quiet Ambition
themes.one_liner: No drama. A merchant who simply wants their business to be great — understated, real, documentary.
themes.core_insight: Polished ads signal advertising. Documentary-style, low-production-feel ads signal authenticity. A merchant who sees a real person in a real shop — not a model in a perfect set — lowers their guard and engages with the content as if it were organic.
themes.NOT: Testimonial ads (proven weak as acquisition). This is NOT a talking-head testimonial. It is candid, observational — the merchant is not speaking to camera.
execution_directions: Overhead shot of a busy counter — hands, POS screen, food. No faces. One line of copy.
A merchant checking their phone at end of day — a StoreHub dashboard notification showing day's sales. No words needed.
Documentary still: empty restaurant, owner setting tables before service, light coming through the window.
A close-up of a POS screen during service — orders flowing in. Shot like a film still.
themes.copy_direction: Minimal. Max 6 words headline. Let the image carry 80% of the message.
themes.hypothesis: Authentic/low-production-feel creative drives higher SQL% than polished brand ads because it reduces ad resistance and attracts merchants who are genuinely evaluating, not just browsing.
themes.known_data: TH bloopers/unexpected opening hooks drove 2-3x video engagement (Hook Rate 0.50% vs 0.15%). Authentic feel is directionally validated in TH. Untested as static in MY.
themes.watch_out: Must still meet brand standards. Logo and CTA required. Do not make it so low-production it looks like an error.

themes.name: The Math
themes.one_liner: Hard, specific numbers that make the cost of inaction impossible to ignore.
themes.core_insight: Vague benefit claims ('save time, save money') are discounted by the brain. Specific numbers force calculation: 'If I'm paying 30% commission and doing RM50k/month, that's RM15k gone every month.' The ad becomes a mirror showing them a number they cannot unsee.
themes.emotional_lever: Financial pain made concrete — triggers loss aversion
themes.NOT: Generic percentage claims without context. 'Save 55%' with no anchoring is weak. The math must be their math.
execution_directions: A comparison: [Their monthly Grab commission] vs [StoreHub monthly fee]. Just two numbers.
A receipt-style breakdown: what they pay per year in commissions, errors, manual overtime vs StoreHub cost.
RM3.40/day — shown as coins, as a drink, as the most affordable thing in their life.
A timeline: 'At RM48,000 renovation cost, your POS is the 1 thing you shouldn't overpay for. RM3,960 with StoreHub.'
themes.copy_direction: Lead with the number. Make it specific to their world (RM, their vertical, their scale). No fluff.
themes.hypothesis: Specific financial numbers (RM3.40/day, 30% commission = RM X) drive lower CPL than feature benefit copy because they create a tangible, calculable cost-of-inaction.
themes.known_data: Price anchor headlines with hardware visual proven in both MY and PH. PHP63/month is the top-performing PH message across 2 quarters. RM3.40/day framing is in the product but undertested as a visual hero.
themes.watch_out: Numbers must be accurate and market-specific. Never use Malaysian pricing in PH ads or vice versa.

themes.name: Competitive Contrast
themes.one_liner: Force a direct comparison — StoreHub vs the alternative — and make the choice obvious.
themes.core_insight: Merchants who are actively evaluating solutions are comparison shopping. An ad that does the comparison for them, clearly and boldly, intercepts this research moment and short-circuits the funnel. The viewer who clicks already has intent.
themes.emotional_lever: Clarity + relief — 'The decision has been made for me'
themes.NOT: Choose Your Fighter (CYF) hardware tier comparison — that's already in the proven library and is a safe pattern. This theme compares StoreHub vs real alternatives: manual processes, GrabFood/FoodPanda, pen-and-paper, expensive competitors.
execution_directions: 'GrabFood takes 30%. StoreHub takes 0.' — Two numbers, full stop.
Split: LEFT = manual stock count at midnight / RIGHT = StoreHub dashboard in 30 seconds.
'Your current setup' (list of 6 disconnected tools with costs) vs 'StoreHub' (one line, one price).
A fake job posting: 'Hiring: Human who manages POS + inventory + loyalty + delivery + reports. OR: StoreHub. From RM3.40/day.'
themes.copy_direction: Make the comparison feel fair, then make the answer obvious. Never attack by name — compare to a behavior or category, not a brand.
themes.hypothesis: Comparison framing drives higher CTR because it forces active evaluation, and higher SQL% because people who engage with comparisons are already in a buying mindset.
themes.known_data: CYF hardware comparison: CTR 3.95% MY, 4.86% PH — 4x+ benchmark. This is the single best-performing format in the library. This theme extends the comparison angle beyond hardware tiers.
themes.watch_out: Do not name competitor brands. Compare to behaviors, costs, or categories.

themes.name: Social Proof
themes.one_liner: Real merchants, specific outcomes — not generic testimonials. Data that removes purchase risk.
themes.core_insight: Generic testimonials ('I love StoreHub!') are ignored. Specific outcome proof ('Binq reduced manpower by 2 staff after switching') creates credibility that cannot be faked. The specificity is what makes it believable — and believable proof is the most powerful trust-builder.
themes.emotional_lever: Risk reduction — 'If it worked for someone exactly like me, it will work for me'
themes.NOT: Old-style testimonial quote ads. Those have been proven weak as acquisition. This theme requires specific, named merchants with specific, numbered outcomes.
execution_directions: A merchant's real face + their business name + one specific number: 'Merchants Lane — reduced closing time from 2 hours to 20 minutes.'
'17,218 merchants. 3 countries. 1 POS.' — simple, authoritative, scale as social proof.
Before/after with a real merchant name and their specific metric change.
A wall of logos/names of real F&B businesses in KL that use StoreHub. Density as proof.
themes.copy_direction: Be specific. Name the merchant, name the outcome, name the number. Vague proof is no proof.
themes.hypothesis: Specific outcome social proof (named merchant + measurable result) drives higher SQL% and Win% than product-feature ads because it reduces purchase risk for prospects in late-stage evaluation.
themes.known_data: F&B vertical-specific imagery lifts SQL% ~2x in PH. Testimonial ads failed as acquisition in past but those used low-quality quotes — high-quality outcome proof with real faces + numbers is a fundamentally different product, untested.
themes.watch_out: Requires merchant consent and verified numbers. Do not exaggerate or fabricate metrics.

themes.name: Cultural Pride
themes.one_liner: Speaks to the identity of being a Malaysian/Filipino/Thai business owner — local food, local language, local reality.
themes.core_insight: Most tech ads show the product first. The most resonant ads show the culture first — nasi lemak, boba, halo-halo, pad kra pao. When a merchant sees their food, their language, their neighbourhood represented, the ad stops being an ad and starts being content that belongs in their feed.
themes.emotional_lever: Recognition + belonging — 'This brand understands people like me'
themes.NOT: Generic pan-Asian stock photography. Forbidden by brand guidelines. Must be specific to market: Malaysia ≠ Philippines ≠ Thailand.
execution_directions: MY: Nasi lemak or roti canai as the full-bleed hero. StoreHub branding minimal at bottom. 'Your stall. Our tech.'
PH: Halo-halo or lechon as hero. Tagalog/Taglish copy. '#1 POS for Filipino F&B.'
TH: Thai food hero image. Thai script headline. Local merchant face.
MY: A hawker stall at night market — busy, authentic, recognisably Malaysian. POS visible but not the focus.
themes.copy_direction: Write in the market's primary language. Use local food vocabulary. Reference local business culture (e.g., 'gerai', 'kopitiam', 'karinderia').
themes.hypothesis: Culturally specific imagery (local food as hero, native language, local merchant faces) drives lower CPL through higher volume than generic tech/product ads because it generates stronger scroll-stop rate in the target feed.
themes.known_data: PH: F&B vertical-specific imagery lifted SQL% to 45% vs 20-25% generic. TH: Blooper/unexpected cultural hooks drove Hook Rate 0.50% vs 0.15% benchmark. Malay-language static with local food is explicitly listed as untested high-potential in knowledge base.
themes.watch_out: Must use authentic imagery — real food, real places, real people. Stock photos of generic 'Asian food' will perform no differently than generic ads.

themes.name: Aspirational Self
themes.one_liner: The merchant they want to become — running a great operation, growing, winning, present for what matters.
themes.core_insight: Not every merchant is in acute pain. Some are doing okay but want to do better. Aspiration-first ads speak to growth identity, not problem identity. They attract a different, often higher-quality segment: merchants who are already functional but want to scale.
themes.emotional_lever: Growth ambition + pride in progress — 'I want my business to look like that'
themes.NOT: Generic lifestyle imagery with a POS in the background. The aspiration must be specific to what a merchant genuinely wants: more revenue, more time, less stress, a second location — not a vague idea of 'success'.
execution_directions: A merchant checking a clean StoreHub dashboard showing record monthly sales. One line: 'Best month yet.'
A photo of a second location opening. 'StoreHub grows with you.'
A merchant leaving work at 6pm instead of midnight. 'Reports close themselves now.'
An owner teaching a new staff member in under 5 minutes. 'Zero training time. Just open and sell.'
themes.copy_direction: Speak to where they want to be, not where they are. Future tense or present tense describing the dream state.
themes.hypothesis: Aspiration-first creative attracts higher-intent prospects who are already functional and actively looking to grow, resulting in higher Win% (close rate) even if CTR and CPL are not the strongest.
themes.known_data: No direct aspiration-first test in current dataset. Indirect signal: English language drives highest Win% in MY — aspirational messaging tends to be English-dominant in Malaysian context.
themes.watch_out: Aspiration must feel earned and real — not a luxury lifestyle that is unrelatable. The merchant should look like a merchant, not a model.

experiment_structure.description: How to run theme experiments systematically
rules: Test 2-3 themes per iteration — never test all 8 simultaneously (budget gets too thin per theme to reach statistical significance)
Each theme gets minimum 2 creative variations (different executions of the same angle — not different themes)
All variations produced in all 3 formats: 1080x1080, 1920x1080, 1080x1920
Minimum 1,000 impressions and 7 days before calling a result
Winning threshold: 10%+ lift on primary KPI vs iteration control
Kill threshold: Primary KPI >50% below target after 1,000 impressions
Theme winners are evolved (new executions of same angle), not replaced immediately
Theme losers are retired for that market — may be retested in different market if untested there
priority_order: T2 — New Chapter (most directly relevant to current 55% off new business campaign)
T4 — The Math (price anchors already proven — test as visual theme)
T5 — Competitive Contrast (extend the proven CYF angle beyond hardware tiers)
T7 — Cultural Pride (high-potential, explicitly flagged untested in knowledge base)
T1 — Pain Amplification (extends proven question-hook angle into visual)
T6 — Social Proof (requires real merchant data — run when assets are ready)
T8 — Aspirational Self (long-term brand play — lower urgency than conversion themes)
T3 — Quiet Ambition (test in TH first where authentic hooks have proven engagement)

recommended_first_experiment.rationale: These three cover the emotional (milestone), rational (numbers), and comparison angles. All three have directional data supporting them. They are the highest-probability themes for the current 55% off new business campaign.
recommended_first_experiment.control: Current best-performing safe format from knowledge base (CYF hardware split)

theme_to_format_affinity.note: Some themes naturally suit certain formats. Use this as a starting point, but test across all formats.

T1_pain_amplification.reason: Full-screen vertical forces immersion in the scene — makes the pain feel inescapable

T2_new_chapter.reason: Tall format mirrors the emotional weight of a milestone moment — cinematic quality

T3_quiet_ambition.reason: Square documentary feel matches organic feed content format

T4_the_math.reason: Numbers need breathing room — square gives space without distraction

T5_competitive_contrast.reason: Side-by-side comparisons work naturally in landscape — wide format enables the split

T6_social_proof.reason: Trust signals are most credible in the native feed format

T7_cultural_pride.reason: Full-bleed local food photography is most impactful at full vertical — feels like food content

T8_aspirational_self.reason: Landscape communicates scale and success — wider frame feels more expansive
